# Knowledge System Architecture

> **Version**: 1.7.3 | **Last reviewed**: 2026-04-02

## Overview

PARA Workspace v1.7.0+ introduces the **Knowledge System** â€” persistent, cross-session memory for AI agents via Knowledge Items (KIs). KIs are curated, distilled knowledge that persists across conversations and projects.

KIs live **outside** the workspace, in the KI Store managed by the Antigravity platform (`~/.gemini/antigravity/knowledge/`). PARA Workspace governs KI operations (schema, rules, lifecycle workflows) without owning the storage layer.

## Architecture

```text
â”Œâ”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”    â”Œâ”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”
â”‚  KI Store                   â”‚    â”‚  PARA Workspace             â”‚
â”‚  ~/.gemini/antigravity/     â”‚â—€â”€â”€â”‚  Governance Layer:          â”‚
â”‚  knowledge/                 â”‚    â”‚  â”œâ”€ ki.schema.json          â”‚
â”‚  â”œâ”€ {slug}/                 â”‚    â”‚  â”œâ”€ heuristics.md (H10)     â”‚
â”‚  â”‚  â”œâ”€ metadata.json        â”‚    â”‚  â”œâ”€ rules/knowledge.md      â”‚
â”‚  â”‚  â”œâ”€ timestamps.json      â”‚    â”‚  â””â”€ workflows/knowledge.md  â”‚
â”‚  â”‚  â””â”€ artifacts/           â”‚    â”‚                             â”‚
â”‚  â””â”€ .archived/              â”‚    â”‚  Index Layer:               â”‚
â”‚     (retired KIs)           â”‚    â”‚  â””â”€ .para/knowledge/        â”‚
â”‚                             â”‚    â”‚     â”œâ”€ index.md (12-col)    â”‚
â”‚  (platform-managed)         â”‚    â”‚     â””â”€ reports/audit-*.md   â”‚
â””â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”˜    â””â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”˜
```

## KI Types

### System KIs (`para_*`)

Managed by PARA Workspace. Source of truth: `repo/templates/knowledge/`.

- Slug prefix: `para_` (reserved, enforced by KR3)
- Owner: `para`
- Lifecycle: template â†’ `./para install` â†’ KI Store â†’ `./para update` (auto-sync)
- Example: `para_workspace_architecture_standards`

### User KIs

Created by users/agents. No prefix restrictions (except `para_` which is reserved).

- Owner: `user`
- Lifecycle: `/knowledge [topic]` â†’ KI Store
- Scope: `workspace`, `project`, or `ecosystem`
- Naming convention: `project_{name}` for project-specific, or descriptive topic slug
  - Example: project `my-app` â†’ `project_my_app`
  - See [Slug Naming Convention](./ki-anatomy.md#slug-naming-convention-v173)

## Context Flow (v1.7.2)

```text
Session Start                    During Session                 Session End
â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€                    â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€                 â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€
Platform auto-injects      â†’     Agent uses injected data  â†’   /end suggests
KI summaries into context        for scope matching             KI create/update
                                 (no file I/O needed)

/open Step 2.7:                  /plan Phase E:                /end Step 4.7:
"From injected KI data,          pitfall â†’ Risks               cross-ref session
match scope to project"          playbook â†’ Phase refs          with KI titles
```

Before v1.7.2, workflows read `.para/knowledge/index.md` to discover KIs. This was redundant because the platform already injects KI summaries. v1.7.2 removes these file reads.

## Schema

Each KI contains a `metadata.json` with graph-ready fields:

| Field           | Type       | Description                                  |
|:----------------|:-----------|:---------------------------------------------|
| `title`         | string     | Descriptive title                            |
| `summary`       | string     | â‰¤800 chars                                   |
| `version`       | string     | KI content version                           |
| `scope`         | enum       | `workspace` / `project` / `ecosystem`        |
| `domain`        | string     | Open taxonomy (e.g., `workspace`)            |
| `purpose`       | enum       | `context` / `reference` / `pitfall` / `playbook` |
| `owner`         | enum       | `para` (system) / `user`                     |
| `para_version`  | string     | PARA version at creation/update              |
| `tags`          | string[]   | Free-form tags                               |
| `references`    | object[]   | File paths, conversation IDs                 |
| `relates_to`    | string[]   | KI â†” KI relationships (graph edge)           |
| `code_refs`     | string[]   | KI â†” Code relationships (graph edge)         |
| `concepts`      | string[]   | KI â†” Concept relationships (graph edge)      |

Full schema: [`kernel/schema/ki.schema.json`](../../kernel/schema/ki.schema.json)

## Index Schema (v1.7.2)

`.para/knowledge/index.md` â€” user-facing reference, auto-generated by `/knowledge`:

```markdown
| # | Title | Slug | Owner | Scope | Domain | Purpose | PARA Ver | Arts | Refs | Modified | Health |
```

12 columns. Abbreviations: Owner = `para`/`user`, Scope = `ws`/`proj`/`eco`.

## Taxonomy

Two-axis classification: **domain** (open) Ã— **purpose** (fixed enum).

```text
              context      reference    pitfall     playbook
            â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€ â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€ â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€ â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€
workspace   PARA arch    kernel specs update bugs audit
engineering tech stack   API docs     dep gotchas deploy
operations  infra setup  CI/CD ref    env traps   rollback
content     writing std  style guide  SEO traps   publish
strategy    org context  roadmap      scope creep planning
...         (open â€” user-defined domains)
```

## Knowledge Graph Seed (v1.7.2)

System KI templates now include **file-level `code_refs`** (16 entries) that map which files are affected when modifying the knowledge system. This is the foundational data for future Knowledge Graph capabilities:

```text
v1.7.2 (now)           v1.8.0 (Department)     v2.x (Context Intelligence)
â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€           â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€       â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€
code_refs seed    â†’    Department KIs with  â†’  Auto-discover code_refs
(16 files manual)      domain-based routing    Semantic search on graph
relates_to empty       relates_to populated    Dependency traversal
```

## Governance

| Rule             | Description                                       |
|:-----------------|:--------------------------------------------------|
| **KR1** Write    | Only `/knowledge` workflow can create/modify KIs  |
| **KR2** Approval | All KI operations require user confirmation       |
| **KR3** Namespace| `para_*` prefix reserved for system KIs           |
| **KR4** Summary  | Summary â‰¤ 800 characters                          |
| **KR5** Recovery | All operations undoable (archive, not delete)     |
| **KR6** Lifecycle| System KIs sync from repo templates via CLI       |

Validation: **H10** (11 clauses) in `kernel/heuristics.md`.

## Workflow Integration

| Workflow       | Integration                                 | Version |
|:---------------|:--------------------------------------------|:--------|
| `/knowledge`   | Full lifecycle: create, update, audit, sync | 1.2.0   |
| `/open`        | Platform-injected KI context, scope match   | 1.7.1   |
| `/plan`        | Pitfall â†’ Risks, Playbook â†’ Phase refs      | 1.7.1   |
| `/end`         | Suggests creating/updating KIs from session | 1.7.1   |
| `/brainstorm`  | Option F: Extract insight as KI             | 1.7.1   |
| `/retro`       | Graduates cross-project patterns to KIs     | 1.7.1   |
| `/learn`       | KI suggestion after lesson capture          | 1.7.1   |

## System KI Template Sync

```text
repo/templates/knowledge/     CLI install/update       KI Store
para_workspace_*/         â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â†’  ~/.gemini/antigravity/
â”œâ”€ metadata.json              compare para_version    knowledge/para_*/
â””â”€ artifacts/                 merge strategy:         â”œâ”€ metadata.json
                              template wins metadata   â”œâ”€ timestamps.json
                              union merge references   â””â”€ artifacts/
                              keep user artifacts
```

CLI `update.sh` auto-syncs system KIs using a dual-gate strategy (v1.7.3):

1. **Version gate**: compare `para_version` in template vs installed metadata
2. **Content hash gate**: compare file hash (catches same-version hotfixes)

If either gate detects a change, the template overrides the installed KI (idempotent â€” no-op when both match).

# Architecture Overview

> **Version**: 1.4.0

## The Three Entities

PARA Workspace operates through three distinct entities:

### 1. Repo (Source / Governance)

The GitHub repository containing the canonical rules, tools, and templates.

```
para-workspace/
â”œâ”€â”€ kernel/        # Rules (invariants + heuristics + schemas)
â”œâ”€â”€ cli/           # Tools (init, scaffold, migrate, install)
â”œâ”€â”€ workflows/     # Reference workflows (no state)
â”œâ”€â”€ templates/     # Project/task templates + profile presets
â”œâ”€â”€ docs/          # Developer documentation
â””â”€â”€ examples/      # Reference implementations
```

**Key constraint**: The repo NEVER contains user data (`Projects/`, `Areas/`, `Resources/`, `Archive/`).

### 2. Workspace (Runtime Instance)

A local directory generated by `para init`. This is where the user and agent work daily.

```
workspace/
â”œâ”€â”€ Projects/      # Active work
â”œâ”€â”€ Areas/         # Stable knowledge
â”œâ”€â”€ Resources/     # References & tools (includes kernel snapshot)
â”œâ”€â”€ Archive/       # Cold storage
â”œâ”€â”€ .agents/        # Agent runtime guardrails
â””â”€â”€ .para-workspace.yml  # Runtime metadata
```

**Key constraint**: The workspace is a standalone instance. Multiple workspaces can exist from one repo.

### 3. Agent (Execution Environment)

The AI agent (Antigravity) attaches to a workspace and operates within its rules.

- Reads `.agents/rules/` for guardrails
- Reads `Resources/ai-agents/kernel/` for system rules
- Operates within `Projects/` for daily work

## Data Flow

```
Repo â”€â”€(para init)â”€â”€> Workspace â”€â”€(agent attach)â”€â”€> Agent Runtime
       <â”€â”€(para install)â”€â”€         <â”€â”€(agent operations)â”€â”€
```

- `para init`: Generates workspace from repo + profile + language
- `para install`: Syncs kernel + workflows from repo to workspace
- `para migrate`: Upgrades workspace to newer kernel version
- Agent operations: Read/write within workspace `Projects/`, `Areas/`, etc.

## Version Tracking

| Location                                | Tracks                     |
| --------------------------------------- | -------------------------- |
| Repo `VERSION`                          | Kernel version             |
| Workspace `.para-workspace.yml`         | Kernel + workspace version |
| Workspace `Resources/ai-agents/VERSION` | Snapshot version           |

# Rule Layers & Trigger Index Architecture

> **Version**: 1.6.2 | **Last reviewed**: 2026-03-24

## Overview

Rules are `.md` files that govern AI Agent **behavior** â€” boundaries, priorities, and discipline. Unlike Workflows (execution steps), Rules define constraints the agent must follow.

Three key properties:

1. **Layered** â€” Kernel â†’ Global â†’ Project
2. **Progressive Disclosure** â€” load only when needed, never all at once
3. **Trigger Index** â€” lightweight tables mapping actions to rule/skill files with priority levels
4. **Context Recovery** â€” Defense-in-Depth guardrails against context truncation
5. **Proactive Trigger Check** (v1.6.2) â€” scan triggers BEFORE any side-effect

## Rule Layers

```
â”Œâ”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”
â”‚ Layer 1: KERNEL (Immutable)                  â”‚
â”‚ Resources/ai-agents/kernel/invariants.md     â”‚
â”‚ â†’ 11 invariants (I1-I11), read only by audit â”‚
â”œâ”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”¤
â”‚ Layer 2: GOVERNED RULES (Global, from repo)  â”‚
â”‚ .agents/rules/*.md                            â”‚
â”‚ â†’ 10 rules, synced via ./para install/update â”‚
â”‚ â†’ Apply to ALL projects in workspace         â”‚
â”œâ”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”¤
â”‚ Layer 3: PROJECT RULES (Per-project)         â”‚
â”‚ Projects/<name>/.agents/rules/*.md            â”‚
â”‚ â†’ Custom rules, supplement (not override)    â”‚
â”‚ â†’ Declared via rules.md trigger index        â”‚
â””â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”˜
```

### Layer 1: Kernel

- **File:** `invariants.md` â€” 11 hard rules, change requires RFC + MAJOR bump
- **Read by:** Only `/para-audit` (full-scan) â€” the sole workflow allowed to read the full kernel

### Layer 2: Governed Rules (Global)

Synced from `catalog.yml` by `./para install` or `./para update`.

| Rule                         | Purpose                                           | Loaded when                |
| :--------------------------- | :------------------------------------------------ | :------------------------- |
| `agent-behavior.md`          | Communication, language, noise reduction          | Always (lightweight)       |
| `governance.md`              | Kernel boundaries â€” restrict system modifications | Touching kernel/ or .para/ |
| `context-rules.md`           | Context loading order + trigger index protocol    | Every session              |
| `hybrid-3-file-integrity.md` | Hot Lane + compress-not-delete + /end sync        | Operating on tasks/        |
| `para-discipline.md`         | PARA classification enforcement                   | Creating/moving files      |
| `artifact-standard.md`       | Document format standards                         | Creating artifacts         |
| `naming.md`                  | File/branch/commit naming                         | Creating new files         |
| `vcs.md`                     | Git best practices                                | Committing/pushing         |
| `versioning.md`              | SemVer policy                                     | Version bumps              |
| `exports-data.md`            | Data export safety                                | Exporting/sharing          |

### Layer 3: Project Rules

- **Location:** `Projects/<name>/.agents/rules/`
- **Not synced from repo** â€” user-created via `/para-rule add`
- **Supplement** global rules, never override

## Trigger Index (Two-Tier Progressive Disclosure)

The system uses **index files** so the agent knows which rules AND skills exist and when to load them:

**Tier 1a: Workspace Rules Index** (`.agents/rules.md`) â€” ALWAYS READ

```markdown
| Rule                    | Trigger                                           | File                             | Pri |
| :---------------------- | :------------------------------------------------ | :------------------------------- | :-- |
| Governance              | Touching kernel/, .para/ â€” MUST NOT modify        | rules/governance.md              | ðŸ”´  |
| VCS                     | Git commit, push, merge, branch, tag, PR          | rules/vcs.md                     | ðŸ”´  |
| ...                     | ...                                               | ...                              | ðŸŸ¢  |
```

**Tier 1b: Workspace Skills Index** (`.agents/skills.md`) â€” ALWAYS READ (v1.6.2+)

```markdown
| Rule          | Trigger                              | File             | Pri |
| :------------ | :----------------------------------- | :--------------- | :-- |
| Code Style    | Editing src/, writing new components | code-style.md    | ï¿½   |
| Deploy Safety | Deploying, editing CI/CD configs     | deploy-safety.md | ï¿½   |

## File Guards

| File pattern       | MUST re-read     | Reason                        |
| :----------------- | :--------------- | :---------------------------- |
| `CHANGELOG.md`     | code-style.md    | Must follow commit convention |
| `deploy/`, `.env*` | deploy-safety.md | Safety checks before deploy   |
```

> **File Guards** (v1.5.4): Optional section in project `rules.md`. Extends the global guards from `agent-behavior.md` Â§4. Agent reads both global + project guards during Context Recovery.

### Loading Flow (v1.6.2)

```
/open
  â†“
Step 2.5a: Read .agents/rules.md (workspace rules index) â€” ALWAYS
  â†’ Memorize triggers (do NOT read rule files)
  â†“
Step 2.5b: Read .agents/skills.md (workspace skills index) â€” ALWAYS (v1.6.2+)
  â†’ Memorize skill triggers
  â†“
Step 2.5c: agent.rules / agent.skills / has_rules?
  â†’ YES â†’ Read project indices
  â†’ NO  â†’ Skip (workspace indices still loaded)
  â†“
Coding session: agent about to edit repo/
  â†’ Proactive Trigger Check â†’ Match: "Editing repo/" â†’ load dogfooding-policy.md â†’ comply
```

### `agent` Map in project.md (v1.6.2+)

```yaml
agent:
  rules: true    # Gate for /open Step 2.5c (project rules)
  skills: true   # Gate for /open Step 2.5c (project skills)
```

- `agent.rules: true` â†’ `/open` reads project rules index
- `agent.skills: true` â†’ `/open` reads project skills index
- `has_rules: true` â†’ backward compat fallback (deprecated)
- `/para-audit update` Step 5 checks consistency between `agent` map and actual files

## Workflow Coverage

| Workflow      | Rules Index           | Skills Index           | Pre-flight             | Detail                                                        |
| :------------ | :-------------------- | :--------------------- | :--------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `/open`       | âœ… Step 2.5a (ALWAYS) | âœ… Step 2.5b (ALWAYS)  | â€” (IS the loader)      | Workspace: always. Project: if `agent.*: true`                |
| `/plan`       | âœ… Step 2.7 D1-D2     | âœ… Step 2.7 D3          | âœ… Step 0 (v1.6.2)     | D1: workspace. D2: project rules. D3: project skills          |
| `/docs`       | âœ… Step 0             | âœ… Step 0              | âœ… Step 0 (v1.6.2)     | Re-reads rules + skills before doc generation                  |
| `/push`       | âœ… Step 0             | âœ… Step 0              | âœ… Step 0 (v1.6.2)     | Re-reads before git operations                                 |
| `/release`    | âœ… Step 0             | âœ… Step 0              | âœ… Step 0 (v1.6.2)     | Re-reads before release                                        |
| `/end`        | âœ… Step 0             | âœ… Step 0              | âœ… Step 0 (v1.6.2)     | Re-reads before session sync                                   |
| `/backlog`    | âœ… Step 0             | âœ… Step 0              | âœ… Step 0 (v1.6.2)     | Re-reads before backlog mutation                               |
| `/retro`      | âœ… Step 0             | âœ… Step 0              | âœ… Step 0 (v1.6.2)     | Re-reads before archive                                        |
| `/para-audit` | â€”                     | â€”                      | â€”                      | Agent index consistency check (rules + skills vs disk)         |
| `/para-rule`  | â€”                     | â€”                      | â€”                      | CRUD rule management                                           |

## References

- **Rule:** `context-rules.md` Rule #4 â€” Agent Index Loading protocol
- **Workflow:** `/open` Step 2.5a/2.5b/2.5c, `/plan` Step 2.7 D1/D2/D3

# v1.4.0 â€” Repo â†” Workspace Separation & Kernel System

> **Release date:** 2026-02-13

## âš ï¸ Breaking Changes

- **Repo â†” Workspace Separation**: The repo no longer contains `Projects/`, `Areas/`, `Resources/`, `Archive/`. It is now purely governance (kernel, CLI, templates, workflows, docs).
- **`metadata.json` â†’ `.para-workspace.yml`**: Replaced JSON metadata with YAML config.
- **`workspace.md` â†’ merged into `README.md`**: Reduced file count.
- **CLI path changed**: `Areas/infra/cli/` â†’ `cli/commands/`. Entry point: `cli/para`.
- **Workflow path changed**: `Resources/ai-agents/workflows/` â†’ `workflows/` (top-level).
- **Rules extracted into Kernel**: `Resources/ai-agents/rules/` â†’ `kernel/invariants.md` + `kernel/heuristics.md`.
- **Task model changed**: Single `tasks.md` â†’ Hybrid 3-file (`backlog.md` canonical, `sprint-current.md` + `done.md` derived).

## Highlights

- ðŸ§  **Kernel System** â€” Constitution with 10 Invariants and 8 Heuristics
- ðŸ‘¤ **Profile System** â€” 4 presets (dev, general, marketer, ceo)
- ðŸ”§ **CLI Rewrite** â€” All commands rewritten for v1.4 architecture
- ðŸ“– **Documentation Suite** â€” Architecture, kernel, workflows, CLI, migration guides

## Added

- **Kernel System** (`kernel/`):
  - `KERNEL.md` â€” Constitution / supreme law.
  - `invariants.md` â€” 10 hard rules (I1â€“I10) that must not be violated.
  - `heuristics.md` â€” 8 soft conventions (H1â€“H8) for recommended practices.
  - `schema/tasks.schema.md` â€” Hybrid 3-file task model specification.
  - `schema/decision-plan.schema.json` â€” JSON Schema for decision records.
  - `examples/` â€” Compliance test vectors (decisions + tasks).
  - `README.md` â€” Quick reference for all invariants and heuristics.
- **Profile System** (`templates/profiles/`):
  - `general/preset.yaml`, `dev/preset.yaml`, `marketer/preset.yaml`, `ceo/preset.yaml`.
- **New CLI Commands**:
  - `para init [--profile=X] [--lang=X] [--path=X]` â€” Create workspace from repo + profile.
  - `para archive <type>/<name>` â€” Move items to Archive with graduation review.
- **Cross-platform Fix**: All CLI scripts include `normalize_path()` to fix Windows/PowerShell backslash path issues.
- **Documentation** (`docs/`): `architecture.md`, `kernel.md`, `workflows.md`, `cli.md`, `migration.md`.
- **Governance Files**: `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `VERSIONING.md`.

## Changed

- **CLI Rewrite**: All core scripts rewritten â€” `init.sh`, `status.sh`, `migrate.sh`, `install.sh`, `scaffold.sh`.
- **Templates** (`templates/common/`): Project, task, and agent governance templates.

## Fixed (builds 3â€“6)

- **BUG-01**: Permission denied on CLI scripts â†’ `init.sh` now sets `chmod +x`.
- **BUG-02**: Missing install step â†’ `init.sh` now calls `install.sh` automatically.
- **BUG-03**: `install.sh` crash on duplicate files â†’ Added `.bak` backup mechanism.
- **BUG-04**: `para update` path error â†’ Fixed `REPO_ROOT` resolution.
- **BUG-05**: Clone path mismatch â†’ Standardized to `Resources/references/` (lowercase).
- **BUG-08**: Missing `_inbox` directory â†’ `para init` now creates `_inbox/`.
- **Build 4**: Centralized workflows, profile standardization, CLI refactor.
- **Build 5**: `/open` workflow respects `preferences.language`.
- **Build 6**: Profile architecture simplification, `/learn` workflow standardized.

# v1.4.10

## Added

- **New Workflow: `/docs`**: The official Documentation Manager workflow has been added to the governed catalog (`kernel_min: 1.4.10`).
  - **Internal-first design**: Docs are always created in `docs/` and promoted to `repo/docs/` on demand.
  - **Doc Index Pattern**: Automatically generates and maintains a lightweight `README.md` index in the `docs/` folder to save tokens and prevent directory scanning.
  - **Language Adaptation**: Automatically detects the repository's main language and translates/condenses internal native-language documents into English (or the repo's language) when publishing.
  - **4 Actions**: `new` (create doc), `review` (audit freshness), `update` (sync with code), `publish` (copy to repo).

## Changed

- **Version Bump**: Workspace version is now `1.4.10`.
- **Workflow Catalog**: `catalog.yml` updated with the new `/docs` workflow.
- **Documentation**: Updated `workflows.md` to include `/docs` in the Admin category.
- **Documentation Guide**: A new `docs.md` added under `repo/docs/workflows/` illustrating usage of the new workflow.

# v1.4.2 â€” Plan-Driven Development

> **Release date:** 2026-02-26

## Highlights

- ðŸ“‹ **`/plan` Workflow** â€” Create, review, and update phased implementation plans
- ðŸ”— **Plan â†” Backlog Sync** â€” Backlog items mapped to plan phases
- âš¡ **Token-Optimized Context** â€” `active_plan` field enables grep-only plan loading

## Added

- **Workflow: `/plan`** â€” New governed workflow for creating, reviewing, and updating phased implementation plans. Supports `create`, `review`, and `update` actions. Integrates with `/backlog` for phase tracking and cross-referencing.
- **`active_plan` Field** â€” New optional field in `project.md` frontmatter to register the active implementation plan. Enables token-optimized plan context loading in `/open` and `/end` (grep-only, no full plan reads).
- **Backlog Action: `sync`** â€” New action in `/backlog` to synchronize backlog items with plan phases, detecting unmapped tasks and auto-creating entries.
- **Catalog Entry**: Added `plan` to `workflows/catalog.yml` (now 18 total entries).

## Changed

- **Workflow: `/backlog` v1.0.0 â†’ v1.1.0**:
  - `review` shows current Phase context from implementation plan.
  - `update` announces Phase completion when all phase items are done.
  - `add` asks which Phase new items belong to.
  - Template adds optional `Phase` column for plan integration.
  - Added language constraint from `.para-workspace.yml`.
  - Added Plan Integration reference section.
- **Workflow: `/open` v1.0.0 â†’ v1.1.0**:
  - New Step 5: Read plan summary via `active_plan` field (grep-only, token-optimized).
  - Report template adds `ðŸ“ CURRENT PHASE` section with progress tracking.
  - Suggested Actions prioritize tasks from the current phase.
- **Workflow: `/end` v1.0.0 â†’ v1.1.0**:
  - New Step 4: Check Plan Phase Progress via `active_plan` field (grep-only).
  - Adds `Plan Progress` block to session log template.
  - Suggests `/plan update` if scope changed during session.
- **Workflow: `/new-project`**: Added `active_plan` field to project.md template, added `/plan` to Related section.
- **Schema: `project.schema.json`**: Added `active_plan` property (string or null, backward-compatible).
- **Template: `project.md`**: Added `active_plan` field to frontmatter.

# v1.4.3 â€” CLI Fixes & Plan-Aware Workflows

> **Release date:** 2026-02-26

## Highlights

- ðŸ› **CLI Bug Fixes** â€” Fixed `install.sh` kernel version propagation and nested library copying
- ðŸ“ **Profile Templates** â€” Added `/plan` workflow and `plans/` directory to `dev` profile
- ðŸ”„ **`/end` v1.2.0** â€” Automated `active_plan` cleanup when project plan is 100% complete

## Fixed

- **CLI Updater**: Fixed `install.sh` failing to propagate `$KERNEL_VERSION` and crashing script execution due to unhandled `set -e` in `sync_file()`.
- **CLI Workspace**: Fixed `.para-workspace.yml` kernel version not automatically updating during `./para install` or `./para update`.
- **Governed Libraries (Skills)**: Fixed `install.sh` failing to copy nested subdirectories within libraries, effectively allowing complex items like `skills` (e.g., `para-kit`) to correctly sync to `.agents/skills/`.

## Changed

- **Profile Templates**: Added `/plan` workflow and `plans/` directory to the `dev` profile structure.
- **Workflow: `/end` v1.1.0 â†’ v1.2.0**:
  - Added `[done]` optional parameter to the command syntax.
  - New logic: When the `done` keyword is used, the workflow detects if the project's `active_plan` is 100% complete.
  - Automated Action: If 100% complete (or requested via `done`), the agent automatically removes the `active_plan` field from `project.md` to optimize token usage for future sessions.
  - Updated all internal logic to be bilingual-ready.
- **Workflow Version Labels**: Bumped all governed library version references to `1.4.3`.

# v1.4.5 â€” Safety Guardrails & Progressive Disclosure

> **Release date:** 2026-03-02

## Highlights

- ðŸ”’ **Safety Guardrails** â€” Terminal Allowlist protects workspaces from destructive commands
- ðŸ” **Progressive Disclosure** â€” Agents only read lightweight `governance.md`, not the full Kernel Spec
- ðŸ—ï¸ **`/para-audit`** â€” New Macro Assessor workflow to detect structural drift

## Added

- **Workflow: `/para-audit`** â€” New governed workflow functioning as a Macro Assessor to check structural drift against Kernel Specs. It's the only daily workflow allowed to full-scan the Kernel Specs.
- **Progressive Disclosure** â€” Implemented a token-saving model where agents only read the lightweight `governance.md` during regular tasks and only access the comprehensive Kernel Spec during `/plan`, `/para-audit` or when creating a new project.

## Changed

- **Kernel Version**: Bumped to `v1.4.5`.
- **Rule: `governance.md`** â€” Rewritten to be ultra-lightweight (saving thousands of tokens). Integrated **Invariant IDs** (e.g., `[I1 & I8]`) directly into safety rules so the agent can cross-reference invariants without loading the full `invariants.md` spec. Added **Safety Guardrails** (Terminal Allowlist) to protect workspaces.
- **Workflow: `/open`**: Modified to explicitly forbid scanning the Kernel Spec to prevent attention decay and context bloat.
- **Workflow: `/plan`**: Updated to allow selective, on-demand reading of Kernel components (like `invariants.md` or `heuristics.md`) rather than unrestricted scanning.

# v1.4.7 â€” macOS Compatibility & Safe Migration Pipeline

> **Release date:** 2026-03-03

## Highlights

- ðŸŽ **macOS Compatibility** â€” 3 critical fixes for Bash 3.2 and BSD utilities
- ðŸ”„ **Safe Migration Pipeline** â€” `backup_and_copy()` protects user-customized files
- âš¡ **Version Gating** â€” `migrate.sh` skips already-completed migration steps automatically

## Added

- **Workflow: `/backup` Upgrade**: Added `project <name>`, `project-all` targets for backing up project user data (sessions, artifacts, docs, project.md, `.agents/`). **Repos are excluded** â€” they can be re-cloned from GitHub. Extended `metadata` target to include workspace-level sessions from `Areas/Workspace/` (SESSION_LOG, SYNC, audits). Added `What Gets Backed Up?` reference table.
- **Safe Copy Helper**: Added `backup_and_copy()` function to `migrate.sh` â€” creates `.bak` backup before overwriting any user-customized file.
- **Version Gating**: `migrate.sh` now evaluates `--from` version against three gates (`<1.4.0`, `<1.4.1`, `<1.4.6`) using `semver_gte()`. Steps for already-completed migrations are automatically skipped, reducing runtime and eliminating redundant overwrites.
- **Update Pipeline Resilience**: `update.sh` now auto-detects `WORKSPACE_ROOT` if not set (via `.para-workspace.yml` scan). Migration failures are non-fatal â€” `install.sh` always runs even if `migrate.sh` encounters issues.

## Fixed

- **macOS Compatibility (3 critical fixes)**:
  - `cli/para`: Replaced `;;&` (Bash 4+ only) with merged case pattern `help|--help|-h|*)` for Bash 3.2 compatibility.
  - `install.sh`, `migrate.sh`: Replaced `sed -i` (GNU-only) with portable `sed ... > tmp && mv tmp file` approach for BSD compatibility.
  - `init.sh`: Replaced `head -n -1` (GNU-only) with `sed '$d'` for BSD compatibility.
- **Environment Variable Consistency**: Unified `PARA_WORKSPACE_ROOT` â†’ `WORKSPACE_ROOT` across `logger.sh` and `rollback.sh` to match the convention used in all other scripts.
- **Rule Protection**: `migrate.sh` Step 6 no longer uses raw `cp` to overwrite governance rules. All copy operations now use `backup_and_copy()`.

## Changed

- **Kernel Version**: Bumped to `v1.4.7`.

## Windows Note

> If `para update` fails on Windows due to NTFS file locking, the recommended recovery is:
>
> ```cmd
> cd Resources\references\para-workspace
> git checkout -- .
> git pull origin main
> cd ..\..\..
> .\para install
> ```

# v1.4.8 â€” Atomic Rollback, Dry-run Pipeline & README Rewrite

> **Release date:** 2026-03-04

## Highlights

- ðŸ›¡ï¸ **Atomic Rollback** â€” `install.sh` now automatically restores all files if it fails mid-operation
- ðŸ” **Dry-run Mode** â€” Preview `para install` and `para update` changes before applying
- ðŸ“„ **README Rewrite** â€” Installation guide redesigned with platform compatibility table and 2-step setup

## Added

- **Atomic Rollback for `install.sh`** (FEAT-30): Integrated `rollback.sh` into the install pipeline. If `install.sh` fails mid-operation, all modified files are automatically restored to their previous state. Uses `rollback_init` / `rollback_register` / `rollback_commit` lifecycle with `trap EXIT` handler.
- **`--dry-run` for `install.sh`** (FEAT-31): New `para install --dry-run` previews all file sync operations without writing any files or creating backups.
- **`--dry-run` for `update.sh`** (FEAT-31): New `para update --dry-run` skips `git pull` and passes `--dry-run` through the entire pipeline (migrate + install), enabling full update preview.
- **Windows Lock Guard**: `backup_file()` now wraps `cp` in error handling for NTFS file lock scenarios. Rollback error handler includes Windows-specific recovery hint.

## Changed

- **Kernel Version**: Bumped to `v1.4.8`.
- **CLI Help Text**: Updated `cli/para`, `install.sh`, and `update.sh` help output to document `--dry-run` option.
- **Install Header**: Mode display now shows `DRY RUN`, `FORCE`, or `Smart` explicitly.
- **Audit Logging**: `install.sh` now records `OK` or `ROLLBACK` status in `.para/audit.log` via `log_audit`.
- **README Installation Rewrite** (FEAT-33):
  - Added Prerequisites section (Git, Bash, AI Agent)
  - Added Platform Compatibility table (Antigravity âœ…, Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code âšª)
  - Simplified to 2-step install: Clone & Install â†’ Verify
  - Unified Bash commands across Linux/macOS/Windows Git Bash
  - Added `--dry-run` and rollback documentation in Updating section

## Technical Details

### Rollback Lifecycle

```
rollback_init        â†’ Create temp session dir
  â†“
rollback_register    â†’ Copy original file to session (per file, before modification)
  â†“
[install operations]
  â†“
rollback_commit      â†’ Delete session dir (success path)
  OR
trap EXIT            â†’ rollback_execute â†’ restore all registered files (failure path)
```

### Dry-run Pipeline

```
para update --dry-run
  â†“ skip git pull
  â†“ migrate.sh --dry-run  (preview migrations)
  â†“ install.sh --dry-run  (preview file syncs â†’ "Would sync: ...")
  â†“ No files changed
```

### Cross-platform Safety

All CLI scripts verified clean:

- No `sed -i` (incompatible with BSD/macOS)
- No `;;&` (Bash 4+ only)
- No `readarray` / `mapfile` (Bash 4+ only)
- No `declare -A` (associative arrays, Bash 4+ only)
- `backup_file()` guards against NTFS file locks on Windows

## Files Changed

| File                      | Change                                            |
| :------------------------ | :------------------------------------------------ |
| `cli/commands/install.sh` | Rollback integration, dry-run, Windows lock guard |
| `cli/commands/update.sh`  | Dry-run parsing, git pull skip, passthrough args  |
| `cli/para`                | Help text updated                                 |
| `README.md`               | Installation rewrite, badge, roadmap              |
| `docs/README.vi.md`       | Installation rewrite (Vietnamese), badge, roadmap |
| `CHANGELOG.md`            | v1.4.8 entry                                      |
| `VERSION`                 | 1.4.7 â†’ 1.4.8                                     |

# v1.4.9 â€” Centralized Backup & Workspace Cleanup

> **Release date:** 2026-03-04

## Highlights

# v1.5.0

## Added

- **New Workflow: `/update`**: Agent-guided safe workspace update with pre-flight checks and error recovery (`kernel_min: 1.5.0`).
  - **Pre-flight checks**: Validates network connectivity, git status, and version state before updating.
  - **Dry-run preview**: Runs `para update --dry-run` first so users can review changes before applying.
  - **Error recovery**: Built-in diagnosis table for common failures (network, git conflicts, permissions, rollback).
  - **Post-update verification**: Confirms version, migration history, and audit log after update.

- **New Workflow: `/brainstorm`** (Governed): Collaborative ideation with structured output and 5 exit paths (`kernel_min: 1.5.0`).
  - Saves structured analysis to `artifacts/para-decisions/brainstorm-[topic]-[date].md`.
  - **5 exit paths**: Seeds (incubate), Plan (formalize), Backlog (simple tasks), Doc (preserve as reference), Learn (extract reusable knowledge).
  - Integrated with `/plan` Step 2.5 â€” plan auto-discovers recent brainstorm outputs.

- **Project Rules Loading (Progressive Disclosure)**: New Rule #4 in `context-rules.md`.
  - Agent checks for a lightweight `rules.md` index at `Projects/<project>/.agents/rules.md`.
  - Rules are loaded **on demand** â€” only when the current action matches a trigger, not upfront.
  - New template `rules.md` included in project scaffolding.
  - Workflow `/open` updated with Step 2.5 to auto-load project rules index.
  - **Kernel heuristic H2** updated with the lazy-loading protocol definition.

## Fixed

- **`update.sh` skipping migrations**: `CURRENT_VER` was read from `repo/VERSION` (already updated by `git pull`), causing it to always equal `NEW_VER` and skip `migrate.sh`. Now reads from `.para-workspace.yml` (the workspace's actual installed version).
  - **Impact**: `history.log` was not recording updates from v1.4.7 onwards.

## Changed

- **Version Bump**: Workspace version is now `1.5.0`.
- **Workflow Catalog**: `catalog.yml` updated with `/update` and `/brainstorm` workflows.
- **Workflow `/open`**: Added Step 2.5 for project rules index loading. Version bumped to 1.5.0.
- **Workflow `/plan`**: Added Step 2.5 for brainstorm context discovery, renumbered Learnings to Step 2.6. Added `/brainstorm` to Related. Version bumped to 1.5.0.
- **Workflow `/para-rule`**: Added step to update `rules.md` index when adding project-specific rules; updated Context Routing section. Version bumped to 1.5.0.
- **Documentation**: Added `docs/workflows/update.md`, `docs/workflows/open.md`, `docs/workflows/brainstorm.md`, `docs/workflows/plan.md`, `docs/project-rules.md`; updated `docs/workflows.md` and both READMEs.

# Release v1.5.1 â€” Hybrid 3-File Synchronization

> **Date:** 2026-03-11
> **Theme:** "Fast Mode & No Amnesia"

This release finalizes the **Hybrid 3-File Model** architecture, changing how AI Agents and users interact with task management within PARA workspaces.

## ðŸŒŸ Core Features

1. **Auto-Sync `sprint-current.md` (One-way Snapshot)**
   - The `/backlog update` command now automatically scans for tasks with `ðŸš€ ToDo` or `ðŸ”¨ In Progress` statuses and renders/overwrites them into `sprint-current.md`.
   - **Benefit:** Creates an ultra-lightweight "Fast Mode" Focus View that the AI Agent can read frictionlessly daily, eliminating the need to parse massive backlog files and saving thousands of tokens.

2. **Auto-Archive `done.md` (Append-only)**
   - Added automatic completion routing: When a task is marked as `âœ… Done`, it is copied and time-stamped into `done.md`.
   - Added a new **`/backlog clean`** action to perform bulk house-cleaningâ€”sweeping all completed tasks from the backlog into the historical `done.md` bucket in one go.
   - **Benefit:** Maintains an unbloated historical log of project velocity while ensuring the canonical `backlog.md` stays lean and clean.

3. **Context Workflow Updates**
   - **`/open`**: Optimized to prioritize reading `sprint-current.md` instead of the full `backlog.md`. This "Fast Mode" cuts out 90% of token noise when opening a new session.
   - **`/plan` review**: Instead of scanning the backlog for progress, `/plan review` has been rebuilt to read directly from `done.md`. This ensures phase completion is tracked accurately and can trigger project finality automatically.
   - **`/retro`**: Re-engineered to require `done.md` as its mandatory Input Data source for completion and velocity metrics, removing the outdated reliance on scraping scattered session logs.

## ðŸ›  Enhancements

- **Template Improvements (`repo/templates/`):** Full audit and standardization of the "General" Profile (FEAT-25) to align perfectly with root directory structures; synchronized all workflow templates with their active v1.5.1 versions (FEAT-34).
- Kernel Version automations bumped for `project.md` and `.project.yml`.

## ðŸ› Fixes & Polish

- Fixed a missing syntax keyword defect in the `new-project.md` template command structure.

---

**Upgrade Action:** Run `./para update` within your root workspace directory to sync the new engine and architecture.

> **Release Date**: 2026-03-13
> **Kernel**: 1.5.3
> **Theme**: Hot Lane, /end Sync Point, Token Optimization

---

## Summary

This release fundamentally refactors the Hybrid 3-File Architecture. The key insight: `sprint-current.md` was designed as a "Derived Focus View" rendered from backlog, but agents never actually used it that way. In practice, agents read backlog directly and sprint-current sat empty.

**v1.5.3 redefines `sprint-current.md` as a "Hot Lane"** â€” an agent-writable buffer for ad-hoc quick tasks that emerge during coding sessions. All synchronization is consolidated to the `/end` command via "Hot Lane Sync".

# v1.5.4 â€” Defense-in-Depth: Context Recovery & Rule Guards

> **Release Date**: 2026-03-17
> **Kernel**: 1.5.4
> **Theme**: Context Recovery, Rule Priority, Workflow Pre-flight, File Guard Headers

---

## Summary

This release addresses a critical gap: after **context truncation** (checkpoint, sliding window), agents lose all rules loaded at session start and may silently violate constraints. v1.5.4 implements a **4-layer Defense-in-Depth** strategy where each layer covers the gaps of the previous one.

The design was validated by a real-world dogfooding incident: the agent violated `done.md` append-only constraint (C2) during this very session, which led to discovering the "workflow bypass" gap and creating Layer 4 (File Guard Headers).

## Breaking Changes

None. All changes are additive and backward compatible.

## Changes

### Rules

| File                               | Change                                                                                                                                            |
| :--------------------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `rules/agent-behavior.md`          | Section 4: Context Recovery protocol + **File-Level Guards table** (file â†’ required rule map)                                                     |
| `rules/hybrid-3-file-integrity.md` | **C6: File Guard Headers** â€” inline `<!-- âš ï¸ -->` comments as last-resort defense                                                                 |
| `rules/context-rules.md`           | Rules Index format: Priority column + **File Guards format** specification for project rules                                                      |
| `rules.md` (index)                 | Added **Priority column** (ðŸ”´ Critical, ðŸŸ¡ Important, ðŸŸ¢ Standard). Reordered rules by priority. Enhanced VCS and Governance trigger descriptions |

### Workflows

| File           | Change                                                                                            |
| :------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `/open`        | Step 8: **Safety Block** â€” compact rules reminder (~40 tokens) that survives checkpoint summaries |
| `/push`        | Step 0: **Rules Pre-flight** â€” re-read `rules.md` from disk before git operations                 |
| `/release`     | Step 0: Rules Pre-flight                                                                          |
| `/end`         | Step 0: Rules Pre-flight                                                                          |
| `/plan`        | Step 0: Rules Pre-flight                                                                          |
| `/docs`        | Step 0: Rules Pre-flight                                                                          |
| `/backlog`     | Step 0: Rules Pre-flight                                                                          |
| `/retro`       | Step 0: Rules Pre-flight                                                                          |
| `/new-project` | Step 3: **Companion file templates** â€” `done.md` + `sprint-current.md` with guard headers         |

### Documentation

| File                                      | Change                                                    |
| :---------------------------------------- | :-------------------------------------------------------- |
| `docs/architecture/context-recovery.md`   | ðŸ†• New: Defense-in-Depth architecture doc (EN)            |
| `docs/architecture/hybrid-3-file.md` (EN) | C6 reference, guard headers mention, version bump         |
| `docs/reference/project-rules.md` (EN)    | Layer 4 (File Guard Headers), 4-layer list                |
| `docs/workflows/new-project.md` (EN)      | Companion files in tree + checklist                       |
| `README.md` (EN)                          | Flat badges, workspace_framework badge, Antigravity badge |
| `docs/README.vi.md` (VI)                  | Same badge updates                                        |

## 4-Layer Architecture

```
Layer 1: Rule file (agent-behavior.md Â§4)
  â””â”€ Context Recovery protocol + File-Level Guards table
  â””â”€ Covers: workflow bypass (direct edits)
  â””â”€ Type: Passive (depends on agent detecting decay)

Layer 2: Workflow output (/open Safety Block)
  â””â”€ Compact rules reminder in Step 8 report
  â””â”€ Covers: checkpoint truncation (survives in summary)
  â””â”€ Type: Passive (informational)

Layer 3: Workflow pre-flight (Step 0)
  â””â”€ 7 workflows re-read rules.md from disk
  â””â”€ Covers: normal workflow usage after truncation
  â””â”€ Type: Active (force re-read)

Layer 4: File Guard Headers (C6) â­
  â””â”€ Inline <!-- âš ï¸ --> in done.md, sprint-current.md
  â””â”€ Covers: all remaining cases (Proximity Principle)
  â””â”€ Type: Active (agent sees guard before editing)
```

## Token Impact

```
Defense-in-Depth total cost: ~200-275 tokens/session
  L1: ~100 tokens (on-demand rule re-read)
  L2: ~40 tokens  (Safety Block in /open report)
  L3: ~60-105 tokens (Step 0 Ã— 4-7 workflows/session)
  L4: ~0-30 tokens (guard headers per file read)

Overhead: 3-5% of session budget â€” negligible for comprehensive protection.
```

## Dogfooding Validation

The agent violated C2 (wrote directly to `done.md`) during this session while implementing FEAT-47. Root cause analysis:

1. **Context decay** â€” long conversation, rules lost after checkpoint
2. **Workflow bypass** â€” agent edited files directly instead of using `/backlog`
3. **"Helpful bias"** â€” agent tried to complete multiple actions at once

This incident exposed Layer 3's gap (pre-flight only works if workflow is used) and directly led to creating Layer 4 (File Guard Headers) and the File-Level Guards table in Layer 1.

# v1.6.0 â€” Meta-Project & Ecosystem Support

> **Release Date**: 2026-03-20
> **Kernel**: 1.6.0
> **Theme**: Multi-project coordination, cross-project plans, ecosystem governance
> **RFC**: [RFC-0003](../../rfcs/0003-meta-project-governance.md)

---

## Summary

This release introduces **Ecosystem Projects** â€” a meta-project concept that enables multi-project coordination within the standard PARA structure. An ecosystem project (`type: ecosystem`) acts as a coordinator for related satellite projects, holding shared strategy, cross-project plans, and roadmaps â€” but no source code.

Key capabilities:
- **Project types**: `standard` (default) or `ecosystem` (meta-project, no `repo/`)
- **Satellite linking**: bidirectional references via `ecosystem` and `satellites` fields
- **@prefix resolution**: `@my-ecosystem/plans/roadmap.md` resolves across project boundaries
- **Workflow adaptation**: 5 workflows detect ecosystem type and behave accordingly
- **Consistency validation**: `/para-audit` validates ecosystem â†” satellite integrity

# v1.6.2 â€” Unified Agent Index

> **Released:** 2026-03-24 | **Type:** MINOR feature | **FEAT-53**

## Summary

Introduces the **Unified Agent Index** â€” a parallel skills trigger index alongside the existing rules index, a new `agent` map in project schema replacing `has_rules`, and a **Proactive Trigger Check** mechanism that ensures agents scan all trigger tables before performing side-effect actions.

## What's New

### Skills Trigger Index

| Item | Path |
| :--- | :--- |
| Template | `repo/templates/common/agent/skills.md` |
| Workspace copy | `.agents/skills.md` |
| Synced by | `install.sh` (mirrors `rules.md` logic) |

The skills index follows the same Two-Tier Progressive Disclosure pattern as rules â€” agent reads the index (~10 lines) at session start and loads individual skills on demand when triggers match.

### Agent Map in project.md

```yaml
# v1.6.2+ (new)
agent:
  rules: true
  skills: true

# Legacy (deprecated, backward compat kept)
has_rules: true
```

The `/open` workflow checks `agent.rules` first, falls back to `has_rules` for backward compatibility.

### Proactive Trigger Check

Before ANY action that edits files, runs commands, or creates artifacts:

1. Scan workspace `rules.md` trigger table
2. Scan workspace `skills.md` trigger table
3. Scan project trigger tables (if loaded)
4. **IF match found â†’ read the rule/skill file BEFORE acting**

> Principle: Check THEN act â€” never act THEN check.

### Agent Indices Pre-flight (Layer 3)

All 7 workflows with Step 0 now re-read both `rules.md` AND `skills.md`:

- `/plan`, `/docs`, `/backlog`, `/push`, `/release`, `/retro`, `/end`

This guards against attention decay in long conversations â€” even if `/open` loaded indices at session start.

| **Workflow** | `workflows/para-audit.md` v1.3.0 | Agent Index Consistency check |
| **Workflow** | `workflows/docs.md` v1.1.1 | Step 0 Pre-flight |

# v1.6.3 â€” Central Gate

> **Released:** 2026-03-27 | **Type:** PATCH optimization

## Summary

Transforms `project.md` into a **Central Gate** â€” the single source of truth for all context
loading decisions. Eliminates filesystem probes for strategy and roadmap in `/open`, `/plan`,
`/docs`, and `/end` by adding two new optional fields (`strategy`, `roadmap`) and a shared
**Path Resolution Convention** supporting cross-project `@{ecosystem}/` prefix.

Also fixes the Step 2.5c skip bug by splitting agent index loading into two distinct steps
with a **Completion Gate** checklist.

## What's New

### project.md Central Gate Fields

```yaml
# New optional fields (v1.6.3):
strategy: docs/strategy/strategy.md       # or @pageel/docs/strategy.md
roadmap: plans/ecosystem-roadmap.md        # or @pageel/plans/xxx-roadmap.md

# Existing (unchanged):
active_plan: plans/xxx.md                  # or @pageel/plans/xxx.md
```

All three fields support `@{ecosystem}/` prefix for cross-project references.
When null or missing â†’ skip entirely (zero I/O).

### Path Resolution Convention

Shared resolution logic for `strategy`, `roadmap`, and `active_plan`:

| Field        | Base path      | @ prefix resolution                              |
| :----------- | :------------- | :------------------------------------------------ |
| `strategy`   | project root   | `@{eco}/docs/x.md` â†’ `Projects/{eco}/docs/x.md`  |
| `roadmap`    | `artifacts/`   | `@{eco}/plans/x.md` â†’ `Projects/{eco}/artifacts/plans/x.md` |
| `active_plan`| `artifacts/`   | `@{eco}/plans/x.md` â†’ `Projects/{eco}/artifacts/plans/x.md` |

### /open Agent Index Fix (Step 2.5 â†’ 2.5 + 2.6)

Step 2.5 was too long (3 sub-steps under one heading) causing agents to skip the
project-level rules/skills loading. Fix:

- **Step 2.5**: Workspace agent indices only (ALWAYS) â€” ~13 lines
- **Step 2.6**: Project agent indices (CONDITIONAL) â€” separate heading + Completion Gate

The Completion Gate requires agents to verify 4 checks before proceeding:

| # | Check                    | Required |
|:--|:-------------------------|:---------|
| 1 | Workspace rules loaded?  | ALWAYS   |
| 2 | Workspace skills loaded? | ALWAYS   |
| 3 | Project rules resolved?  | IF true  |
| 4 | Project skills resolved? | IF true  |

### Token Savings

| Scenario | Before | After | Savings |
|:---------|:-------|:------|:--------|
| Project without strategy/roadmap (~70%) | ~90 tokens (fs probes) | 0 | -90 |
| Project with both | ~150 tokens | ~80 | -70 |
| `/end` per session | ~80 tokens | ~20 | -60 |

## Templates Changed

| Category | File | Change |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Schema** | `kernel/schema/project.schema.json` | `strategy`, `roadmap` fields added |
| **Template** | `templates/common/project.md` | `strategy: ~`, `roadmap: ~` defaults |
| **Workflow** | `workflows/open.md` v1.6.0 | Step 2.5/2.6 split, Path Resolution, field-gated strategy/roadmap |
| **Workflow** | `workflows/plan.md` v1.6.0 | Roadmap field lifecycle |
| **Workflow** | `workflows/docs.md` v1.2.0 | Strategy field lifecycle |
| **Workflow** | `workflows/end.md` v1.6.0 | Field-gated change detection |

## Catalogs Bumped

- `workflows/catalog.yml`: 4 entries updated (open, plan, docs, end)

## Migration

No migration needed. Fully backward compatible:
- Fields missing from `project.md` â†’ treated as null (skip, zero I/O)
- Existing `active_plan` with `@` prefix continues to work
- No CLI changes required

# v1.6.4 â€” Para-Kit Skill v1.1.0, Recursive Sync & Git Hash Detection

> **Released**: 2026-03-30 | **Kernel**: 1.6.4

## Summary

This release restructures the `para-kit` skill into a lean structure reference (v1.1.0), replaces the 1-level directory sync with a fully recursive `sync_directory_recursive()`, and introduces git commit hash-based change detection in `update.sh` to handle hotfixes without version bumps.

## Features

### FEAT-55: Para-Kit Skill Rewrite (v1.1.0)

- **SKILL.md** rewritten as a 5-section structure reference:
  1. PARA Workspace Structure (4 pillars + project layout)
  2. `project.md` Schema (all v1.6.3 fields including `upstream`)
  3. Quick Reference Card â€” Kernel Governance (I1-I11 + H1-H9 one-liners)
  4. Selection Strategy (CLI vs Workflow routing)
  5. On-demand References (templates + examples)
- **Colocation**: `templates/` and `examples/` now live inside the skill folder for automatic sync
- **Generic examples**: `project-schema-vectors.md` uses fictional project names (acme-platform, my-app)
- **Removed**: `formatting-tables-diagrams.md` duplicate from skill templates (now a governed rule)

### FEAT-56: Recursive Directory Sync in install.sh

- New `sync_directory_recursive()` helper handles arbitrarily nested subdirectories
- Replaces the 1-level `for` loop that could not sync `skills/para-kit/templates/` or `examples/`
- Syncs **all file types** (not just `.md`) â€” supports YAML, JSON, etc.
- Uses `|| true` to prevent `set -e` crashes per `bash-cli-gotchas.md` learnings

## Bug Fixes

### BUG-19: Formatting Rule Not Triggered

- **Root cause**: `formatting-tables-diagrams.md` existed only in the workspace (from a dogfooding experiment) without an entry in `rules.md` or `catalog.yml` â†’ agent never triggered it
- **Fix**: Copied rule to repo, added YAML frontmatter, added entry to `rules.md` index and `catalog.yml`

### BUG-20: update.sh Version Comparison Logic

- **Root cause**: `CURRENT_VER` fell back to `repo/VERSION` which would read the *same file* before and after `git pull`, making versions always equal â†’ migration skipped
- **Fix**: `CURRENT_VER` now reads exclusively from `.para-workspace.yml` (workspace copy), with `0.0.0` fallback for fresh installs

### BUG-21: Hotfixes Not Detected by update.sh

- **Root cause**: Version-only comparison could not detect hotfix commits that don't bump `VERSION`
- **Fix**: Git commit hash comparison (`OLD_COMMIT` vs `NEW_COMMIT`) before/after `git pull`. Version comparison now only gates migration, not sync. `install.sh` ALWAYS runs (idempotent).

## Other Changes

- **backup.md**: Added `skills` backup target (`/backup skills` or `/backup all`)
- **skills.md**: Updated trigger keywords for structure reference role
- **rules.md**: Added Formatting rule entry (11 total rules)
- **catalog.yml**: Para-Kit version 1.0.0 â†’ 1.1.0, kernel_min â†’ 1.6.4
- **update-mechanism.md**: Rewritten in English, added git hash detection + recursive sync sections
- **docs/README.md**: Version bump + formatting rule entry

## Files Changed

| File | Change |
| :--- | :----- |
| `cli/commands/install.sh` | Added `sync_directory_recursive()`, refactored `sync_library()` |
| `cli/commands/update.sh` | Git hash detection, workspace-only version read |
| `templates/common/agent/skills/para-kit/SKILL.md` | Full rewrite (structure reference) |
| `templates/common/agent/skills/para-kit/templates/project-md.md` | New file |
| `templates/common/agent/skills/para-kit/examples/project-schema-vectors.md` | New file (generic) |
| `templates/common/agent/skills/catalog.yml` | Version 1.1.0, kernel_min 1.6.4 |
| `templates/common/agent/rules/formatting-tables-diagrams.md` | Promoted from workspace-only to governed |
| `templates/common/agent/rules/catalog.yml` | Added formatting rule |
| `templates/common/agent/rules.md` | Added Formatting rule entry |
| `templates/common/agent/skills.md` | Updated trigger keywords |
| `templates/common/agent/workflows/backup.md` | Added skills backup |
| `VERSION` | 1.6.3 â†’ 1.6.4 |

# v1.7.0 â€” Knowledge System

> **Release Date:** 2026-04-01
> **Type:** MINOR (new feature + heuristic)
> **Kernel:** H10 added (Knowledge Items)

## Summary

Introduces the Knowledge System for persistent AI agent memory across sessions.
Knowledge Items (KIs) are curated, distilled knowledge that persist in the platform's
KI Store and are automatically injected at session start.

## New Features

### Knowledge Items System

- **KI Schema** (`kernel/schema/ki.schema.json`): Graph-ready schema with domain Ã— purpose
  2D taxonomy, `relates_to`, `code_refs`, and `concepts` fields for future Knowledge Graph.
- **`/knowledge` workflow**: Full lifecycle management â€” dashboard, create, update, audit,
  archive. Includes health scoring, reference validation, and auto-indexing.
- **KI Scope Loading** (`/open` Step 2.7): Field-gated conditional loading of KI index
  with scope matching (workspace/project/ecosystem).
- **KI Suggestion Hooks**: Lightweight hooks in `/end` (Step 4.7), `/retro` (Step 4.5),
  `/brainstorm` (Option F), `/learn` (Step 4.5) for proactive KI creation.
- **KI Health Check** (`/para-audit` Step 5.6): Schema compliance, reference integrity,
  staleness monitoring for all KIs.
- **KI Context in Planning** (`/plan` Step 2.7 Phase E): Pitfall KIs â†’ Risks section,
  playbook KIs â†’ Phase task references.

### Governance

- **H10 Knowledge Items** (11 clauses): Schema conformance, artifact requirements,
  scope rules, slug validation (`^[a-z0-9_]{3,60}$`), namespace separation (para_ prefix).
- **KR1-KR5 Knowledge Rules** (`rules/knowledge.md`): Write gate, user approval,
  namespace boundary, zone restriction, recoverability.

### Infrastructure

- **KI Index** (`.para/knowledge/index.md`): Graph-parseable trigger table for scope
  matching, auto-managed by `/knowledge` workflow.
- **KI Seed Templates** (`templates/knowledge/`): System KIs shipped with repo for
  first-install seeding via `para install`/`para update`.
- **Defense-in-Depth L2**: KI section in `/open` Step 8 safety block survives truncation.

## Bug Fixes

- **BUG-25**: Fixed `/open` grep false-positive for brainstorm pending detection.
  Changed from `grep -l "Pending"` to `grep -l "Decision.*Pending"`.
- **BUG-27**: Fixed `./para update` not removing orphan files when catalog entries
  are deleted (e.g. formatting rule â†’ skill migration). Install now compares
  `Resources/ai-agents/` against repo templates and cleans orphans with backup.

### Migrations

# v1.7.3 â€” Agent Path Convention Fix (BUG-28)

> **Released:** 2026-04-02
> **Previous:** v1.7.2

## Summary

Renamed `.agent/` directory to `.agents/` across the entire codebase to match
Antigravity platform's default convention. Added Antigravity-compatible frontmatter
(`trigger`, `glob`, `description`) to all governed rules.

## Breaking Changes

None â€” `para update` includes automatic migration from `.agent/` to `.agents/`.

## Changes

### Bug Fixes

- **BUG-28:** Fixed `.agent/` vs `.agents/` path mismatch that caused Antigravity UI
  to display rules from a different directory than where PARA workspace stores them.
  All 68 files in the repo have been updated to use `.agents/` consistently.

### Improvements

- **Rule Frontmatter:** All 12 governed rules now include Antigravity-compatible
  frontmatter with `trigger`, `glob`, and improved `description` fields.
  This enables better integration with Antigravity's rule management UI.

- **System KI Sync Gate:** Replaced version-only gate (`CURRENT_VER != NEW_VER`)
  with dual-gate strategy: version comparison + content hash comparison. This
  catches same-version hotfixes that previously would silently skip KI sync.

- **`/update` Workflow:** Added Step 4 suggestion to review System KIs via
  `/knowledge` after workspace update â€” improves KI awareness.

- **Slug Naming Convention:** Added naming guide to `/knowledge` workflow:
  `project_` prefix for project-specific KIs, descriptive slugs for cross-project
  knowledge. Documented in `docs/architecture/ki-anatomy.md`.

### Migration

- **Automatic:** `para update` (via `migrate.sh`) will auto-rename `.agent/` to
  `.agents/` for both workspace root and all project directories.
- **Merge logic:** If both `.agent/` and `.agents/` exist (e.g., user created rules
  via Antigravity UI), contents are merged safely before removing the old directory.

# Development Workflow Guide

> **Version**: 1.5.3 | How the daily, planning, release, and operations workflows fit together.

## Overview

PARA Workspace organizes development into 4 workflow streams:

```
â”Œâ”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”
â”‚                                                                      â”‚
â”‚  0. PLANNING          1. DAILY DEV        2. RELEASE      3. OPS    â”‚
â”‚  â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€         â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€          â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€      â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€  â”‚
â”‚  /plan create         /open               /release        /retro    â”‚
â”‚     â†“                    â†“                   â†“            /inbox    â”‚
â”‚  /backlog sync        [coding + hot lane]                           â”‚
â”‚                          â†“                                          â”‚
â”‚                       /push                                         â”‚
â”‚                          â†“                                          â”‚
â”‚                       /end (sync + plan check)                      â”‚
â”‚                                                                      â”‚
â””â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”˜
```

## Daily Flow

```
/open â†’ [code + hot lane] â†’ /push â†’ /end (sync)
```

- **`/open`**: Loads session log, backlog summary, Hot Lane, current phase.
- **Hot Lane** (`sprint-current.md`): Agent-writable buffer for quick tasks. Write `- [ ]` when tasks emerge, tick `[x]` when done.
- **`/push`**: Commit + push to GitHub.
- **`/end`**: Sole sync point. Hot Lane Sync moves `[x]` â†’ `done.md`, suggests marking strategic tasks Done.

> No need to run `/backlog update` mid-session. `/end` handles all sync.

## Artifacts

```
project.md (active_plan, agent map)
    â†’ Plan (plans/)            â† HOW & ORDER
    â†’ Backlog (backlog.md)     â† WHAT & STATUS
    â†’ Hot Lane (sprint-current.md) â† AD-HOC BUFFER
    â†’ Done (done.md)           â† RECORD (#backlog + #session)
    â†’ Session Log              â† EVIDENCE
    â†’ CHANGELOG                â† PUBLIC RECORD
```

Completed plans archive to `plans/done/` with a completion review alongside.

## CLI: update vs install

| Command          | Action               | Use when                  |
| :--------------- | :------------------- | :------------------------ |
| `./para update`  | `git pull` + install | Need latest from GitHub   |
| `./para install` | Sync local only      | Source already up-to-date |

> âš ï¸ `install` does NOT pull. Use `update` for latest version.

## Best Practices

**DO**: Start with `/open` Â· Commit often with `/push` Â· Quick tasks â†’ `sprint-current.md` Â· End with `/end`  
**DON'T**: Skip `/open` Â· Forget `/end` Â· Run `/backlog update` mid-session Â· Read full plan in `/open`

## Related

- [Planning Guide](./planning.md) â€” Plan + Backlog workflow
- [Workflows](../reference/workflows.md) â€” Catalog and philosophy
- [CLI Reference](../reference/cli.md) â€” Command-line tools

# Knowledge Workflow Guide

> **Version**: 1.7.2 | **Last reviewed**: 2026-04-02

## Overview

`/knowledge` manages Knowledge Items (KIs) â€” persistent cross-session memory for AI agents. This guide covers all 8 operations and how the Knowledge System integrates with other workflows.

## Quick Reference

```text
/knowledge                  â†’ Dashboard (visual table)
/knowledge [topic]          â†’ Smart Create/Update (user KI)
/knowledge system [topic]   â†’ System KI Create/Update
/knowledge system update    â†’ Sync system KIs from repo
/knowledge system defaults  â†’ Init default system KIs
/knowledge audit            â†’ Full health check + report
/knowledge archive [#]      â†’ Retire a KI (Smart Archive)
/knowledge [#]              â†’ View KI details
```

## 1. Dashboard

Displays all KIs in two sections: **System KIs** (`para_*`) and **User KIs**.

Health is calculated per KI:

Health     | Condition
:----------|:-------------------------------------------
âœ… Healthy | Modified <30 days, all refs valid, â‰¥1 artifact
âš ï¸ Stale   | Modified 30-90 days, OR â‰¥1 broken ref
ðŸ”´ Critical| Modified >90 days, OR >50% broken refs

After rendering, automatically saves `.para/knowledge/index.md` (12-column schema + per-KI artifact listing with clickable `file:///` links).

## 2. Smart Create/Update

Fuzzy-matches `[topic]` against existing KI titles. Match >70% â†’ proposes UPDATE. Otherwise â†’ proposes CREATE. Always requires user confirmation (KR2).

**Namespace guard (v1.7.1):** Slugs starting with `para_` trigger System KI mode. User KIs cannot use `para_` prefix.

## 3. System KI Routes

System KI         | Description
:-----------------|:-------------------------------------------
`system [topic]`  | Create/update with version alignment + template baseline
`system update`   | Scan templates â†’ upgrade if `para_version` changed
`system defaults` | Init all default system KIs from templates (skip existing)

> Also triggered automatically by `./para install` and `./para update` CLI hooks.

## 4. Audit

Runs full health check on all KIs. Validates reference integrity, freshness, artifact count. Results saved to `.para/knowledge/reports/audit-YYYY-MM-DD.md`.

## 5. Archive

Moves KI to `knowledge/.archived/` â€” never deletes (KR5). Requires user confirmation (KR2).

## 6. Workflow Integration (v1.7.2)

Workflow      | Integration
:-------------|:--------------------------------------------
`/open`       | Platform-injected KI context, scope match
`/end`        | Suggests KI create/update from session
`/plan`       | Pitfall â†’ Risks, Playbook â†’ Phase refs
`/brainstorm` | Option F: Extract insight as KI
`/retro`      | Graduate patterns to KIs
`/learn`      | KI suggestion after lesson capture

> **v1.7.2:** Workflows use platform-injected data instead of reading `index.md` (0 file I/O).

## 7. Workspace Artifacts

```text
.para/knowledge/
â”œâ”€â”€ index.md              # User-facing KI reference (auto-generated)
â””â”€â”€ reports/
    â””â”€â”€ audit-YYYY-MM-DD.md   # Audit trail
```

# Meta-Project & Ecosystem Guide

> **Version**: 1.6.0 | **Last reviewed**: 2026-03-20

## What is a Meta-Project?

A Meta-Project is a coordination project that manages strategy, roadmaps, and cross-project plans for a group of related projects (an ecosystem). It has **no source code** â€” only documentation and plans.

| Scenario                         | Solution                                  |
|:---------------------------------|:------------------------------------------|
| Single product, single repo      | Standard project (`type: standard`)       |
| Single product, multiple repos   | **Meta-Project** (`type: ecosystem`)      |
| Unrelated products               | No need â€” each project is independent     |

## Creating an Ecosystem

### Using `/new-project --meta`

```
/new-project my-ecosystem --meta
```

This scaffolds an ecosystem project (no `repo/` directory):

```
Projects/my-ecosystem/
â”œâ”€â”€ project.md            â† type: ecosystem, satellites: []
â”œâ”€â”€ artifacts/
â”‚   â”œâ”€â”€ tasks/backlog.md  â† Ecosystem-level backlog
â”‚   â””â”€â”€ plans/            â† Cross-project plans
â”œâ”€â”€ docs/                 â† Strategy, architecture docs
â””â”€â”€ sessions/             â† Session logs
```

### Manual Setup

```yaml
# Projects/my-ecosystem/project.md
---
goal: "Coordinate the product ecosystem"
status: "active"
type: "ecosystem"
satellites:
  - my-app
  - my-lib
  - my-docs
---
```

## Linking Satellites

Each satellite project declares its parent ecosystem:

```yaml
# Projects/my-app/project.md
---
ecosystem: "my-ecosystem"
---
```

`/para-audit` validates bidirectional consistency â€” both sides must reference each other.

## Cross-Project Plans

### Create a shared plan

Place plans in the ecosystem's `artifacts/plans/` directory:

```
Projects/my-ecosystem/artifacts/plans/
â””â”€â”€ feature-rollout.md
```

### Reference from a satellite

Use the `@{ecosystem}/` prefix in `active_plan`:

```yaml
# Projects/my-app/project.md
active_plan: "@my-ecosystem/plans/feature-rollout.md"
```

**Resolution:** `@my-ecosystem/plans/feature-rollout.md` â†’ `Projects/my-ecosystem/artifacts/plans/feature-rollout.md`

Rules:
- `@{name}/` resolves to `Projects/{name}/artifacts/`
- Read-only â€” satellites cannot modify ecosystem files
- Workflows validate the referenced file exists

## Workflow Differences

| Step            | Standard Project | Ecosystem Project                |
|:----------------|:-----------------|:---------------------------------|
| Git status      | âœ… Runs           | â­ï¸ Skipped (no repo/)            |
| Git log         | âœ… Runs           | â­ï¸ Skipped                       |
| Satellites list | âŒ N/A            | âœ… Displayed                      |
| Backlog         | âœ… Read           | âœ… Read (ecosystem-level)         |
| Active plan     | âœ… Read           | âœ… Read                           |

## Schema Reference

| Field         | Type                          | Default      | Description                      |
|:--------------|:------------------------------|:-------------|:---------------------------------|
| `type`        | `"standard"` \| `"ecosystem"` | `"standard"` | Project type                     |
| `ecosystem`   | `string` \| `null`            | `null`       | Parent ecosystem (for satellite) |
| `satellites`  | `string[]` \| `null`          | `null`       | List of satellite project IDs    |
| `active_plan` | `string`                      | `""`         | Supports `@{ecosystem}/path`     |

All fields are optional â€” existing projects work without changes.

## FAQ

**Does an ecosystem project have a Git repo?**
No. Ecosystem projects have no `repo/` â€” they only contain strategy docs, plans, and backlogs. Source code lives in satellites.

**Can a satellite belong to multiple ecosystems?**
Currently no. The `ecosystem` field is single-valued.

**Do I need an ecosystem for a single project?**
No. Ecosystems are only useful when you have â‰¥2 related projects that need coordination.
